scope: Survey plausible future serving families only. Codex remains authority on actual architecture and no runtime integration is authorized here.

facts: Current LM Studio v1 docs expose model load/unload and inference but no inspected LoRA/adapter request parameter.
Upstream feature requests for inference-time LoRA adapter support remain open in inspected lmstudio-ai/lms and mlx-engine repositories.
options.consequence: Do not assume the existing RIC LM Studio provider can hotswap a PEFT adapter today. Recheck official docs and local capabilities at integration time.

facts: llama.cpp provides tooling to apply LoRA adapters to a base GGUF and export a merged GGUF.
A historical LM Studio issue describes a Qwen3 fine-tune created by merging an Axolotl LoRA and converting the result to GGUF before serving it in LM Studio.
tradeoffs_to_audit: No in-place adapter hotswap; switching effectively means switching model artifact or model instance.
Derived artifact must retain explicit provenance to base model plus adapter version/config.
A/B qualification remains possible if base and merged artifacts are separately loadable, but operational identity differs from adapter activation.

facts: Current llama-server documentation exposes GET/POST /lora-adapters, startup --lora options and a per-request lora field with adapter id/scale.
This would preserve a single base server with explicit adapter selection rather than require permanent merging.
options.current_risk: An open July 2026 llama.cpp issue reports prompt-cache reuse across requests with different per-request LoRA configurations, causing output contamination. Any RIC evaluation involving adapter switching must falsify this exact failure or isolate cache/server instances until upstream behavior is proven safe.
other_tradeoffs_to_audit: Compatibility of Qwen3 adapter conversion to GGUF and the exact training target modules.
AMD backend performance/stability on the user's workstation.
API compatibility with RIC's current provider transport and reasoning-off contract.
Effective adapter identity and cache invalidation observability.

facts: vLLM supports serving LoRA adapters as model names and documents runtime /v1/load_lora_adapter and /v1/unload_lora_adapter endpoints.
vLLM supports AMD ROCm on Linux and documents gfx1100/gfx1101 hardware families, with current ROCm wheels for selected ROCm versions.
vLLM does not support Windows natively; WSL is the relevant Windows-host path.
current_risks_and_limits: vLLM warns that runtime LoRA updating carries security risks and should be used only in an isolated, fully trusted environment.

The inspected hardware page names Radeon RX 7900 series for gfx1100/gfx1101 rather than explicitly listing RX 7800 XT; shared gfx target is not sufficient proof of supported or stable operation on this exact card.
A local feasibility test is mandatory before considering provider migration.

decision_principles: Do not change serving backend merely because one backend exposes a nicer LoRA API.
Compare semantic correctness, AMD stability, VRAM/RAM, latency, API compatibility, reasoning control, structured-output behavior, observability, security and rollback.
The first behavioral LoRA experiment does not require a production serving decision; PEFT/Transformers can remain an isolated training/evaluation path until the roadmap integration gate.
A runtime path must identify the effective base model and adapter or derived-model provenance unambiguously.
For the first RIC experiment, one adapter only remains the preferred functional scope; multi-adapter serving complexity is not a product requirement.
freshness_rule: All external capability claims in this audit must be reverified immediately before a Codex integration audit because these projects evolve rapidly.
